Sharding strategies for growing datasets

Sharding splits a dataset across several machines so that no single node has to hold all of it. The choice of partition key decides almost everything else about the system.

Hash partitioning

Hashing the key spreads rows evenly and is simple to reason about. The cost is that range scans have to touch every shard, because adjacent keys land in unrelated places.

Adding a node reshuffles a large fraction of the data unless consistent hashing is used.

Range partitioning

Range partitioning keeps adjacent keys together, which makes scans cheap and hotspots likely. A monotonically increasing key sends every write to one shard.

Rebalancing

Splitting a hot range into two is the usual remedy, and it is why range partitioned stores keep a directory of range boundaries.
